reason: This PR adds a per-unit subunit declaration (kind + target headcount) and nothing that reads it: no layout path, no render path, no sim path consumes the two new fields yet, so a recorded battle would be byte-identical to one recorded on main. That is not an assertion -- it was measured. 24 state JSONs across 3 scenarios (the default 5v5 battle, anti-cav-square, all-out-attack) were dumped on the merge-base and again on this branch; stripping exactly the two added dump fields with jq and normalizing both sides gives 24/24 byte-identical files, and two negative controls (strip nothing; strip only one of the two) each report 24/24 DIFFERING, so the comparison demonstrably discriminates. The only existing debug overlay that tints per-soldier internal state, Settings.show_engaged_highlight, renders engaged_soldier_indices() and has no connection to the declaration, so there is no visual precedent to reuse either. When a consumer lands (subunit-level cohesion, sub-unit orders), that PR gets the clip.
